summary: Darwin's Journey has players sending expedition teams around the Galapagos on a worker-placement/pick-up-and-deliver engine, fulfilling contracts, collecting species, and managing a ship route while a tense action-claiming mechanism forces tough ordering decisions. It's a rich, modern heavy euro with a strong sense of forward momentum and satisfying engine-building.
praised: Strong sense of progression and multiple viable strategies
criticised: Heavy rules overhead and long teach
Analysis paralysis potential with many simultaneous tracks
Some find the theme thin dressing over mechanisms
Long playtime for a full 4-player game

interaction.detail: Players compete for limited worker-placement spots and race to complete contracts before others, with claimed actions blocking rivals from the same spot that round. Most of the board (map, action spaces) is shared, while each player also manages their own ship, contracts, and personal tableau.

scoring.why: Points accrue from completed contracts, exploration/discovery tiles, reputation track position, and end-game set bonuses as separate categories.
scoring.how_you_win: You place workers to gather resources, move your ship to explore the islands, and fulfill contracts for reputation and rewards; the player with the most points from combined contracts, exploration, and bonuses at the end wins.
